request.description: Train an I3 intervention candidate with angularly continuous inverse-kinematic branch errors and explicit per-branch joint-limit feasibility margins, while preserving the baseline reward, task mechanics, target distribution, and hold semantics.
request.rationale: I2 identified a negative-bearing approach and branch-selection shortfall, including training-supported radii, while settled trajectories preserved the complete hold. This controlled fresh run changes only the policy representation: each analytic branch is represented by sine/cosine joint errors to remove angular wrap discontinuities and a normalized minimum joint-limit margin to expose branch feasibility. Reward, training target range, PPO configuration, and hold mechanics remain unchanged so any phase-specific change can be attributed to the representation at the level supported by the comparison.

request.description: Run a controlled paired I3 evaluation of the baseline T1:checkpoint-100352 and angularly continuous branch-feasibility intervention T2:checkpoint-100352 over the complete official target distribution.
request.rationale: T2 completed the representation intervention, but training success and reward cannot determine whether negative-bearing approach reliability improved or whether settling and the complete uninterrupted hold were preserved. Evaluate both candidates on the same 200 independent episode seeds drawn from the official radius and full-bearing distribution. The research evaluator records first entry, settling, post-settling interruptions, longest uninterrupted hold, timeout distance, and total success under the unchanged complete-hold semantics; paired comparisons isolate the intervention effect on identical targets.

request.outcome: M3 provides a decision-sufficient negative answer to I3. On the shared 200-episode official-distribution development panel, the baseline T1 achieved 192/200 successes (96.0%) while the angularly continuous, branch-feasibility-aware T2 achieved 129/200 (64.5%), with 6 intervention wins versus 69 baseline wins and a -31.5 percentage-point success difference. The intervention did not reduce the targeted negative-bearing approach failures: T2 had 27 negative-bearing failures versus 8 for T1. Phase diagnostics likewise show degradation before settling: T2 never entered tolerance in 59 episodes versus 5 for T1, and failed to establish settling in 70 versus 8. Post-settling behavior was not preserved: T2 had 3 settled episodes with interruptions and 1 settled episode whose longest hold was below 100 steps, versus 2 and 0 for T1. Both candidates had a maximum uninterrupted hold of 100 steps, but T2 reached that criterion in only 129 episodes. The explicitly sine/cosine angular-error and joint-limit-margin representation therefore is not a credible route to the 196/200 objective under this training recipe and materially degrades the complete task outcome.
request.reason: The controlled paired M3 evidence measures negative-bearing approach outcomes, settling outcomes, post-settling interruptions, longest uninterrupted hold, and total success on the complete official radius and bearing distribution using shared episode seeds. It rejects the tested intervention as a route toward the human goal and answers I3 at the decision resolution for which it was opened.
